categories.name: Data sourcing and analysis universe
categories.definition: How the raw dataset is loaded and what population of rows is taken as the starting universe before any variable is built.
categories.criterion: It names the source/scope of the input rows themselves; if it drops rows for a defined reason it belongs to sample_and_missing instead.

categories.name: Skin-tone exposure construction
categories.definition: How the two rater codings are combined into a skin-tone measure and whether/where that measure is cut into groups for the primary analysis.
categories.criterion: It sets the exposure used by the main analysis; an alternative exposure spec framed as a robustness refit goes to sensitivity_analysis.

categories.name: Red-card outcome definition
categories.definition: How the red-card information is turned into the analysis outcome, e.g. collapsing counts into a binary any-red flag.
categories.criterion: It defines what is being predicted/compared; anything about the exposure or covariates is elsewhere.

categories.name: Row inclusion and missing-data handling
categories.definition: Which observations enter the analytic cohort and how missing or implausible values are resolved (dropping, complete-case, imputation, error filtering).
categories.criterion: The decision changes which rows are kept or fills their missing values; transforming/encoding present-valued variables goes to covariate_construction.

categories.name: Covariate building, encoding, and selection
categories.definition: How adjustment variables are derived, transformed, encoded, and which set of columns is admitted into the model.
categories.criterion: It shapes the covariates/adjustment set assuming values are present; if its main effect is excluding rows it goes to sample_and_missing.

categories.name: Unadjusted comparisons and data-quality diagnostics
categories.definition: Any descriptive statistic, crude group comparison, or reliability/balance check computed outside the adjusted model.
categories.criterion: The number is a raw summary or diagnostic not derived from the fitted primary model; model-derived estimates go to effect_measure or inference.

categories.name: Primary model specification
categories.definition: The choice and fitting of the main regression that produces the adjusted skin-tone effect.
categories.criterion: The act establishes the primary model; a refit whose purpose is changing the SE method or an alternative spec goes to inference or sensitivity_analysis.

categories.name: Effect measure and estimand
categories.definition: On what scale and by what method the skin-tone effect is expressed (odds ratio, average marginal effect, g-computation risk difference).
categories.criterion: It concerns the point estimate/scale of the effect; the uncertainty around it goes to inference.

categories.name: Uncertainty quantification and significance
categories.definition: How standard errors, confidence intervals, and p-values are obtained (robust SEs, bootstrap, delta method) and how significance is declared.
categories.criterion: The decision produces or interprets uncertainty around an estimate; producing the estimate itself goes to effect_measure or primary_model.

categories.name: Robustness and sensitivity refits
categories.definition: Alternative specifications run explicitly to test whether the primary finding holds (dropping subgroups, alternate exposure cuts, stratified refits).
categories.criterion: It is framed as an alternative-to or check-on the primary analysis ('instead of', 'refit', 'sensitivity'); the primary definition itself lives in its own category.

result.note: A few items answer two questions at once (1 restricts rows AND checks inter-rater reliability; 6 selects columns AND drops missing rows); each was placed by its dominant consequence. The lone significance-threshold decision (454) is folded into inference as interpretation of uncertainty rather than a one-item category.
